mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE > 0.5pp in 3 months) signals labor market deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (above 3.0%) indicate stagflation risk, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: High residential construction (HOUST > 550) signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST > 550.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 98.0) indicates manufacturing weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 98.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong residential construction (HOUST > 550) and high consumer spending (RSAFS > 350000) jointly signal robust growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST > 550 and RSAFS > 350000.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production (INDPRO > 100) indicates strong manufacturing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) triggers central bank tightening concerns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.
